Never use linter suppression as\nthe main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.\n\n## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)\n\n### Source-faithfulness checks\n\nFor this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean\nstatement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before\napplying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions\n`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed\nsource-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the\ncorresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.\n\nReject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,\nrepair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,\nor arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as\npositivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal\nencodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when\nmathematically load-bearing.\n\nReviewers should also inspect `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` links.  A source-labelled\nblueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction\ntheorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.\nAuxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the\nremark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.\n\n## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)\n\n### Companion document\n\n> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues\n> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the\n> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still\n> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,\n> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default\n> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).\n> Consult it alongside this file during review.\n\n### Project paper-realignment protocol\n\nThe canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions\n`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as\nfollows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in\n`AGENTS.md`):\n\n> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a\n> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`\n> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be\n> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The\n> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof\n> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the\n> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a\n> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or\n> conditional helper\n> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.\n> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge\n> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.\n\n### Axiom policy\n\nWhen an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,\nprefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`\ndeclaration, and add a regression check (for example a\n`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen\nthe axiomatic base.\n\nThis preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper\ntheorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a\ncaller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a\nproof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\nconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\nfaithful to the paper.\n\n### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization\n\nThis is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or\ntheorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,\nmaking them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.\n\nSigns to watch for:\n\n- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,\n  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's\n  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)\n- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types\n  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions\n- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical\n  semantics (e.g., a \"projective measurement\" definition that does not enforce\n  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)\n- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be\n  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything\n- Definitions that \"work\" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to\n  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,\n  incompatible universes)\n\nWhen reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of\nthis?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the\nscaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks\nprogress rather than enabling it.\n\n### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift\n\nA theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker\nif its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.\nChanging a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is\nstrongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a\ndocumented mathematical necessity.\n\nThe most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an\nextra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional\ntheorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not\nrepair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named\n`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,\ngeneric `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those\nassumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.\n\nConditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet\nbe closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a\nnamed lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional\nhelper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named\nobligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show\nthat it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or\n`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled\nblueprint theorem with `\\leanok`.\n\nExisting bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs\nfor reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a\nstrengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the\nbridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is\nto restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a\ntracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.\n\nNot every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed\nto encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model\ninstances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be\nfaithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These\nconditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is\nmathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate\nstep of the source proof.\n\nFor every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Source-statement proof gaps\n\n**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read\n[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a\nproof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation\nstructure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why\nconditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a\ntracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.\n# Lean Proof-Evasion Anti-Patterns\n\nCatalog of subtle proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks\n(`sorry`-free, no forbidden tactics, all axioms standard) yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics. Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\ncodebase.\n\n## Catalogue\n\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\n\n---\n\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\n\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\nPR [#491].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\n\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content\ncannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation\nto be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open\nunder a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as\nan extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof\ndebt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not\nthe preferred shape for new work.\n\nA signature passes the smell test if:\n\n- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the\n  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and\n- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*\n  theorem, not a trivially-false one.\n\n### Related issues and patterns\n\n- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker\n- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue\n- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by\n  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)\n- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern\n- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation\n\n---\n\n## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand\n\n**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The \"mathematical\ncontent\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\nissues [#477], [#494].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\nanywhere in Lean.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\n  directly.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\n\n```lean\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\n\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) :\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\n\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n  · intro α β\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\n  ...\n```\n\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\ndefinition equals itself.\n\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\n\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\n\n### How to fix it\n\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\n2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those\n   concrete objects.\n3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib\n   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`\n   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).\n4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\n\n---\n\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\n\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \"precondition not met.\" Downstream\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\nfunction. See issue [#495], related to [#307].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a\nnon-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about \"the output\" is\nproved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a\nlater theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition\ntype-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original\nprecondition failed.\n\nThe paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:\n\"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`.\" The Lean should\nmatch.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.\n- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.\n- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,\n  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.\n- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.\n- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial\n  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.\n\n### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)\n\nUntil PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:\n\n```lean\n/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/\nnoncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]\n    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=\n  match g with\n  | some p => p.poly\n  | none   => 0\n```\n\nThe consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange\ninterpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. If the support contained\na `none`, the interpolant silently pretended that slice evaluated to zero.\nThe paper's Lagrange step is quantified over *eligible* slices only, so the\nLean API should carry `∀ i ∈ support, (g i).isSome` as a hypothesis; instead\nit carried nothing, and the theorem technically type-checked on inputs for\nwhich its conclusion was meaningless.\n\n**Current status:** resolved. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,\nthreads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into\n`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset\nas `InterpolationSupportWitness` so the arbitrary choice and its proof fields\nare visible at call sites.\n\n### Acceptable uses of this pattern\n\nNot every default branch is a castle. `Inhabited` / `Nonempty` instances\nthat provide a canonical inhabitant (e.g., the zero polynomial for\n`Nonempty (Polynomial params)`) are plumbing, not proof. The test is: **does\nany theorem mention the output?** If a theorem says \"the output satisfies\nP\", and P is not trivially satisfied by the sentinel, the fallback is\nsmuggling a precondition.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPick one of:\n\n1. **Make the precondition explicit.** Add `(h : eligible input) :` to the\n   signature. Let Lean's type system enforce that non-eligible inputs cannot\n   be passed.\n2. **Return an `Option`.** The `none` result forces every caller to handle\n   the case, so theorems about \"the output\" now quantify only over the\n   `some` branch.\n3. **Restrict the domain.** Instead of `(x : X) → Y`, take `(x : {x : X //\n   P x}) → Y`. Common for finite-support Lagrange-style constructions where\n   the subtype is computable via `Finset.filter`.\n\n### Classical-logic dependencies\n\nA sibling smell in this pattern: `DecidablePred` / `DecidableEq` instances\nthat silently use `Classical.dec` to fill in decidability that should be\nconstructive. The historical `interpolationEligibleSandwichFamily`\nimplementation was exactly such a case: it used `open Classical in ...` to\ngate a predicate that is actually decidable by a finite-support check. PR\n#561 fixed that example by adding `interpolationEligible_decidablePred`.\nThose classical instances are acceptable only when the predicate is genuinely\nnon-constructive; if a constructive instance is plausible, write it, don't\nbottom out in `Classical.dec`. See [#495] for the full catalogue of\nclassical-logic uses in `LDT/Pasting/`.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#307] — placeholder Lagrange coefficient (original fallback tracker)\n- [#495] — the full pasting-interpolation catalogue\n\n---\n\n## A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials\n\n**Smell.** A theorem of the shape `∃ x, P x` is closed by picking\n`x := default`, `x := 0`, `x := 1`, or `x := Classical.arbitrary`, where the\npaper names a *specific, non-trivial* `x` and derives `P x` from real\nstructure. The Lean claim is *mathematically* weaker because the Lean\ntheorem guarantees less than the paper's (it proves some-trivial-thing, not\nthe-specific-paper-thing). See [#449] for the full ledger.\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem name matches a paper lemma but the witness has been cheapened\ninto a placeholder. Downstream theorems that inspect the witness get `0` or\n`default`, which is almost always useless. Consumers that \"use\" the lemma\nare really using the trivial `∃` and cannot proceed past the first attempt\nto pin the witness down.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `refine ⟨default, ?_⟩` / `exact ⟨default, ...⟩` / `refine ⟨0, ?_⟩` /\n  `exact ⟨1, ...⟩` inside a proof of a paper-cited existential.\n- `letI : Inhabited X := ⟨Classical.arbitrary X⟩` followed by a `let x :=\n  default`.\n- `Classical.arbitrary` / `Classical.choice` / `Nonempty.some` in proof\n  bodies (as opposed to typeclass definitions).\n- Identifier suffix `...Witness := default` on a bundled output.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom the ledger in [#449]:\n\n- `lem:sdp` / `sdp` — primal witness is `T := default` (a zero\n  submeasurement) and dual witness `Z := 1`. The paper requires a specific\n  feasible pair; the Lean version proves only that some arbitrary pair exists,\n# Proof Frontier Review\n\nThis document gives a checklist for reviewing Lean changes that introduce or\nthread structure fields in the formalization. Its purpose is to prevent a\nwell-typed bookkeeping layer from being mistaken for a mathematical construction\ntheorem.\n\nThe central distinction is this:\n\n- An **obligation discharger** derives a mathematical object or relation from\n  the hypotheses appearing in the paper or blueprint.\n- An **external residual** records a missing obligation discharger explicitly,\n  with a named issue and a statement of the mathematical obstruction.\n- A **bookkeeping conversion** changes the form or namespace of an already\n  available object without deriving a new mathematical fact.\n\nAll three forms can be legitimate. The review problem is to identify which one\nhas been added, and to make sure the prose, blueprint tags, and issue status say\nthe same thing.\n\n## Why Source-Level Holes Are Not Enough\n\nThe number of occurrences of `sorry` in the source is only a kernel-level\nmetric. It does not determine the mathematical frontier. A proof can be\n`sorry`-free while still assuming the object that the paper asks one to\nconstruct, for example by adding a field to a structure and proving the next\ntheorem by projecting that field.\n\nFor the LDT development this distinction matters most near the main theorem,\nthe main induction step, self-improvement, orthonormalization, and\nprojectivization. In these regions, a single displayed statement in the paper\nusually depends on several intermediate constructions. Closing one local source\nhole may only move the remaining obligation into an input structure.\n\n## Reviewer Checklist\n\nBefore approving a PR that adds or modifies a structure field in a type named\nwith a suffix such as `Input`, `Residual`, `BridgeInputs`, `Witness`,\n`Statement`, `Conclusion`, or `Obligations`, check the following points.\n\n1. **Classify each new field.** State whether the field is produced in the PR,\n   remains an external residual, or is only a bookkeeping conversion.\n2. **Name the obligation discharger.** If the field is produced, cite the exact\n   Lean theorem that derives it from the paper hypotheses. If no such theorem\n   exists, keep the parent mathematical issue open and link a native sub-issue\n   for the missing obligation.\n3. **Check the blueprint frontier.** For work near `mainFormal`, Section 6,\n   self-improvement, orthonormalization, or projectivization, inspect\n   `blueprint/dep_graph_document.html` after building the blueprint. Let $\\\\{A^{x,y_1,y_2}_{a_1,\\\\,a_2}\\\\}$ be a family of projective measurements with outcomes $(a_1, a_2) \\\\in \\\\mathcal R_1 \\\\times \\\\mathcal R_2$ such that for $i \\\\in \\\\{1,2\\\\}$,\\n   373\\t\\t\\\\begin{equation}\\\\label{eq:pasting-1}\\n   374\\t\\t\\tA^{x,y_1,y_2}_{a_i} \\\\ot \\\\Id \\\\simeq_\\\\delta \\\\Id \\\\ot (G_i)^x_{[\\\\operatorname{eval}_{y_i}(\\\\cdot)=a_i]}\\n   375\\t\\t\\\\end{equation}\\n   505\\t\\\\label{sec:types}\\n   506\\t\\n   507\\tThe question distribution of the Pauli basis test is \\\\emph{typed}: each question is a pair consisting of a type, drawn together with the other player's type from the edges of a fixed \\\\emph{type graph}, and a question content, drawn from a CL distribution determined by the pair of types.\\n   508\\t\\n   509\\t\\\\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]\\\\label{def:typed-cl-functions}\\n   510\\t\\t\\\\uses{def:cl-func}\\n   511\\t\\tLet $\\\\mathcal T$ be a finite set (the \\\\emph{type set}) and let $V$ be $\\\\F^n$ for some integer $n \\\\ge 0$. More generally, for an integer $k$ and tuples $m = (m_1,\\\\ldots,m_k)$, $q = (q_1,\\\\ldots,q_k)$, $d = (d_1,\\\\ldots,d_k)$, let $\\\\mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d,k)$ denote the set of measurements $G = \\\\{G_{g_1,\\\\ldots,g_k}\\\\}$ such that for each $i \\\\in \\\\{1,\\\\ldots,k\\\\}$, the outcome index $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i\\\\colon \\\\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \\\\to \\\\F_{q_i}$ of individual degree at most $d_i$.\\n   108\\t\\\\end{definition}\\n   109\\t\\n   110\\tQuantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \\\\emph{total} degree was claimed by Natarajan and Vidick, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test by Vidick; there is a known gap in the soundness analysis of that test, and it is not used here. The statement below is the form most directly useful in what follows.\\n   111\\t\\n   112\\t% The paper states this result in a theorem environment with the label lem:ld-soundness.\\n   113\\t% We keep both the environment and the label verbatim for cross-reference fidelity.\\n   114\\t\\\\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree test]\\\\label{lem:ld-soundness}\\n   115\\t\\t\\\\uses{def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:ld-win-predicate, def:ld-meas, def:projective-strategy-general, def:tensor-product-value, def:povm-distance, def:bracket}\\n   116\\t\\tThere exists a function\\n   117\\t\\t\\\\[\\n   118\\t\\t\\t\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}(\\\\eps, q, m, d, k) = a\\\\,(dmk)^a \\\\bigl(\\\\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}\\\\bigr)\\n   119\\t\\t\\\\]\\n   120\\t\\tfor universal constants $a \\\\ge 1$ and $0 < b \\\\le 1$ such that the following holds. For all $\\\\eps > 0$ and every parameter tuple $\\\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in Definition~\\\\ref{def:ld-game} (so $q$ is an admissible field size and $m$ divides $q$), and for all projective strategies $(\\\\psi, A, B)$ that succeed with probability at least $1-\\\\eps$ in the game $\\\\mathcal G^{\\\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\\\mathsf{ldparams}}$, there exist measurements\\n   121\\t\\t\\\\[\\n   122\\t\\t\\tG^w \\\\in \\\\mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d,k)\\n   123\\t\\t\\\\]\\n   124\\t\\ton $\\\\hilb_w$ for $w \\\\in \\\\{\\\\mathrm A,\\\\mathrm B\\\\}$, where by slight abuse of notation $m$, $q$, $d$ denote the constant tuples $(m,\\\\ldots,m)$, $(q,\\\\ldots,q)$, $(d,\\\\ldots,d)$ of length $k$, such that\\n   125\\t\\t\\\\begin{align*}\\n   126\\t\\t\\tA^{\\\\mathsf{Point},\\\\, u}_{a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k} \\\\ot I_{\\\\mathrm B}\\n   127\\t\\t\\t&\\\\approx_{\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}}\\n   128\\t\\t\\tI_{\\\\mathrm A} \\\\ot G^{\\\\mathrm B}_{[(g_1(u),\\\\ldots,g_k(u)) = (a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k)]}\\\\;,\\\\\\\\\\n   129\\t\\t\\tG^{\\\\mathrm A}_{[(g_1(u),\\\\ldots,g_k(u)) = (a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k)]} \\\\ot I_{\\\\mathrm B}\\n   130\\t\\t\\t&\\\\approx_{\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}}\\n   131\\t\\t\\tI_{\\\\mathrm A} \\\\ot B^{\\\\mathsf{Point},\\\\, u}_{a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k}\\\\;,\\\\\\\\\\n   132\\t\\t\\tG^{\\\\mathrm A}_{g_1,\\\\ldots,g_k} \\\\ot I_{\\\\mathrm B}\\n   133\\t\\t\\t&\\\\approx_{\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}}\\n   134\\t\\t\\tI_{\\\\mathrm A} \\\\ot G^{\\\\mathrm B}_{g_1,\\\\ldots,g_k}\\\\;,\\n   135\\t\\t\\\\end{align*}\\n   136\\t\\twhere $\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}} = \\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}(\\\\eps,q,m,d,k)$, all three approximations are with respect to the state $\\\\ket{\\\\psi}$, and the bracket notation for post-processed outcomes is that of Definition~\\\\ref{def:bracket}. When $\\\\gamma = 0$ the verifier checks commutation directly by asking for both bits simultaneously; when $\\\\gamma = 1$ the verifier checks anticommutation by playing the Magic Square game, using Theorem~\\\\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.\\n   239\\t\\n   240\\t\\\\begin{definition}[Admissible parameters]\\\\label{def:admissible}\\n   241\\t\\t\\\\uses{def:admissible-size}\\n   242\\t\\tThe tuple $\\\\mathsf{qldparams} = (q,m,d)$ is \\\\emph{admissible} if $q$ is an admissible field size (Definition~\\\\ref{def:admissible-size}) and $m$ divides $q$.\\n   243\\t\\\\end{definition}\\n   244\\t\\n   245\\t\\\\begin{definition}[Question distribution of the Pauli basis test]\\\\label{def:pauli-question-distribution}\\n   246\\t\\t\\\\uses{def:admissible, def:ld-question-distribution, def:ms-game, def:cl-func, def:cl-dist, def:graph-distribution}\\n   247\\t\\t% Admissibility of the full tuple is required here, not only the divisibility m | q:\\n   248\\t\\t% the source parametrizes the Pauli basis test by the tuple qldparams introduced\\n   249\\t\\t% together with Definition def:admissible (references/qpbt-paper/\\n   250\\t\\t% 08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-1075), and both the fixed binary\\n   251\\t\\t% identification of F_q used by the map chi and the trace tr in eq:gamma-value\\n   252\\t\\t% require q to be a power of 2.\\n   253\\t\\tThe game $\\\\mathcal G^{\\\\mathrm{pauli}}$ (also $\\\\mathcal G^{\\\\mathrm{pauli}}_{\\\\mathsf{qldparams}}$) is parametrized by an admissible tuple $\\\\mathsf{qldparams} = (q,m,d)$ (Definition~\\\\ref{def:admissible}): admissibility makes $q$ a power of $2$, so that the field $\\\\F_q$, its fixed identification with binary strings (Chapter~\\\\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}), and the trace $\\\\tr\\\\colon \\\\F_q \\\\to \\\\F_2$ used by the win predicate below are defined, and it provides the divisibility $m \\\\mid q$ required by the index map $\\\\chi$ of Definition~\\\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}.    205	def ensure_pr_comment(number: int, marker: str, body: str) -> int:
   206	    """Create or update the single PR comment carrying *marker*.
   207	
   208	    The marker (an HTML comment) is the idempotency key: an existing comment
   209	    is PATCHed in place; after an ambiguous POST failure the list is re-read
   210	    and an adopted comment is not re-posted.

   213	    existing = _find_comment(number, marker)
   214	    if existing is not None:

   216	            payload={"body": full}, mutation=True, idempotent=True)
   217	        return existing
   218	    try:
   219	        created = api(f"issues/{number}/comments", method="POST",
   220	                      payload={"body": full}, mutation=True)
   221	        return int(created["id"])
   222	    except LayerError:

   243	    """Post one COMMENT review bound to *commit_id*; marker-idempotent.
   244

   246	    COMMENT review; adverseness travels in the ``local-review/summary`` status,
   247	    not in a review state.  Returns ``"exists"`` or the new review id.

   250	        if row.get("commit_id") == commit_id and marker in (row.get("body") or ""):
   251	            return "exists"
   252	    payload = {"commit_id": commit_id, "event": "COMMENT",
   253	               "body": _marked_body(marker, body)}
   254	    try:

   256	                      payload=payload, mutation=True)

   258	    except LayerError:
   259	        for row in api(f"pulls/{number}/reviews", paginate=True):
   260	            if row.get("commit_id") == commit_id and marker in (row.get("body") or ""):

   269	def merge_pr(number: int, sha: str) -> str:
   270	    """Merge PR *number* iff its head is exactly *sha*; verify topology.
   271	
   272	    The REST ``sha`` parameter makes GitHub reject the merge when the head
   273	    moved — the atomic exact-head guard, independent of the gh CLI version.
   274	    Returns the merge commit SHA after verifying it has exactly two parents
   275	    with the frozen head second.
   276	    """
   277	    put_error = ""
   278	    try:
   279	        api(f"pulls/{number}/merge", method="PUT",
   280	            payload={"sha": sha, "merge_method": "merge"}, mutation=True)
   281	    except LayerError as exc:
   282	        put_error = str(exc)  # fall through: the read-back below is the authority
   283	    pr = pr_view(number)
   284	    if not pr.get("merged"):
   285	        state = pr.get("state")
   286	        head = (pr.get("head") or {}).get("sha")
   287	        detail = f"; merge call said: {put_error[:400]}" if put_error else ""
   288	        raise LayerError(
   289	            f"PR #{number} did not merge (state={state}, head={head}, "
   290	            f"expected {sha}){detail}")
   291	    merge_commit = pr.get("merge_commit_sha") or ""
   292	    commit = api(f"commits/{merge_commit}")
   293	    parents = [p.get("sha") for p in commit.get("parents") or []]
   294	    if len(parents) != 2 or parents[1] != sha:
   295	        raise LayerError(
   296	            f"PR #{number} merge commit {merge_commit} has parents {parents}; "
   297	            f"expected two with head {sha} second — someone else merged?")
   298	    return merge_commit

   313	def issue_create(title: str, body: str, labels: tuple[str, ...] = (),
   314	                 parent: int | None = None, key: str | None = None) -> int:
   315	    """Create an issue; validate labels; optionally link as a sub-issue.
   316	
   317	    With *key*, a ``<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: ... -->`` marker is embedded and
   318	    an ambiguous create failure adopts the existing issue instead of
   319	    duplicating it.
   320	    """
   321	    check_bracket_free(title, "issue title")
   322	    if labels:
   323	        known = set(list_labels())
   324	        missing = sorted(set(labels) - known)
   325	        if missing:
   326	            raise LayerError(
   327	                f"labels not in the repository: {missing} — create them on "
   328	                f"GitHub first (gh label create) or drop them")
   329	    marker = f"<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: {key} -->" if key else None
   330	    full_body = f"{marker}\n{body}" if marker else body
   331	    # Adoption never returns early: the parent link below must run even when the
   332	    # issue already exists (a prior run may have died between create and link).
   333	    number = _find_issue_by_marker(marker) if marker else None
   334	    if number is None:
   335	        payload: dict = {"title": title, "body": full_body}
   336	        if labels:
   337	            payload["labels"] = list(labels)
   338	        try:
   339	            created = api("issues", method="POST", payload=payload, mutation=True)
   340	            number = int(created["number"])
   341	        except LayerError:
   342	            if marker:
   343	                number = _find_issue_by_marker(marker)
   344	            if number is None:

   351	def _find_issue_by_marker(marker: str) -> int | None:
   352	    rows = api("issues?state=all&sort=created&direction=desc", paginate=True)

   356	        if marker in (row.get("body") or ""):
   357	            return int(row["number"])

     2	"""The one GitHub layer for ``local/bin`` — a thin, fail-closed wrapper over ``gh``.
     3	
     4	GitHub is the single source of truth for issues, PRs, CI evidence (commit
     5	statuses on the exact head SHA), review verdicts (COMMENT reviews bound to a
     6	commit id), and merges (REST merge guarded by an exact-SHA match).  This module
     7	is the only place workflow scripts talk to GitHub, as a Python import or via
     8	its CLI (``gh_common.py <subcommand> ...``) from shell.
     9	
    10	Design rules (local/protocols/issues-prs.md):
    11	
    12	* At most one write mutation per invocation of a helper; ambiguity after a
    13	  failed write is resolved by re-reading state and adopting, never by
    14	  repeating the mutation.  Writes that are idempotent by content (statuses,
    15	  close-PATCH) may be retried blindly.
    16	* Everything uses ``gh api`` (raw REST), so no feature of a modern ``gh`` CLI
    17	  is required — the exact-SHA merge guard is the REST ``sha`` parameter, not a
    18	  CLI flag.
    19	* Fail closed: a network failure after retries raises; no local fallback
    20	  record is ever written.
    21	
    22	Environment: ``MIPSTARRE_GH`` (gh binary; default ``gh`` on PATH, then
    23	``~/.local/bin/gh``), ``MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO`` (``owner/repo``; default
    24	parsed from the ``github`` remote of the primary checkout).
    25	"""
    26	
    27	from __future__ import annotations
    28	
    29	import argparse
    30	import json
    31	import os
    32	import re
    33	import shutil
    34	import subprocess

    50	_TRANSIENT_RE = re.compile(
    51	    r"(?i)(timed? ?out|connection|temporar|unavailable|network|reset by peer|"
    52	    r"tls|eof|http (?:429|5\d\d)|rate limit|bad gateway|service unavailable)"
    53	)

    55	_REMOTE_RE = re.compile(r"github\.com[:/]([^/]+/[^/\s]+?)(?:\.git)?$")

    58	def gh_bin() -> str:
    59	    override = os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_GH")

    72	    override = os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO")

    90	def run_gh(args: list[str], *, input_text: str | None = None,
    91	           mutation: bool = False, idempotent: bool = False,
    92	           retries: int = 3) -> str:
    93	    """Run ``gh`` and return stdout; raise ``LayerError`` on final failure.
    94	
    95	    A non-idempotent mutation is attempted exactly once — the caller owns
    96	    ambiguity recovery by re-reading state.  Reads and idempotent mutations
    97	    retry on transient failures with linear backoff.
    98	    """
    99	    attempts = 1 if (mutation and not idempotent) else max(1, retries)
   100	    env = dict(os.environ, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED="1", GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER="1",
   101	               NO_COLOR="1", GH_PAGER="cat")
   102	    last_err = ""
   103	    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
   104	        proc = subprocess.run(
   105	            [gh_bin(), *args], input=input_text,
   106	            capture_output=True, text=True, env=env,
   107	        )
   108	        if proc.returncode == 0:
   109	            return proc.stdout
   110	        last_err = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout or "").strip()
   111	        if attempt < attempts and _TRANSIENT_RE.search(last_err):
   112	            time.sleep(5 * attempt)
   113	            continue
   114	        break
   115	    raise LayerError(f"gh {' '.join(args[:3])}... failed: {last_err[:2000]}")

   118	def api(path: str, *, method: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None,
   119	        paginate: bool = False, mutation: bool = False,
   120	        idempotent: bool = False, absolute: bool = False):
   121	    """Call the REST API under ``repos/<slug>/`` (or an absolute *path*).
   122	
   123	    Pagination is manual (``?per_page=100&page=N``) so nothing here depends on
   124	    a modern ``gh``.  Returns parsed JSON (``None`` for an empty response).
   125	    """
   126	    full = path if absolute else f"repos/{repo_slug()}/{path}"

   128	    def one(page_path: str):
   129	        args = ["api", page_path]
   130	        if method:
   131	            args += ["-X", method]
   132	        input_text = None
   133	        if payload is not None:
   134	            args += ["--input", "-"]

   136	        out = run_gh(args, input_text=input_text, mutation=mutation,
   137	                     idempotent=idempotent)

   141	        return one(full)

   146	    while True:
   147	        batch = one(f"{full}{sep}per_page={PAGE}&page={page}")
   148	        if not batch:
   149	            break
   150	        rows.extend(batch)
   151	        if len(batch) < PAGE:
   152	            break
   153	        page += 1
   154	    return rows

    13	argv+stdin to a spool and answers from a canned route table, so every test here
    14	runs offline, needs no ``gh`` installed, and asserts on the *wire* contract —
    15	the route, the method and the JSON payload — rather than on a mock's call list.
    16	An unmatched route fails the call: a test that forgets to declare one sees it.

    58	FAKE_GH = '''#!/usr/bin/env python3
    59	"""Stand-in for the gh CLI: log every call, answer from a canned route table."""
    60	import json
    61	import os
    62	import re
    63	import sys
    64	
    65	argv = sys.argv[1:]
    66	method = argv[argv.index("-X") + 1] if "-X" in argv else "GET"
    67	path = argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else ""

    69	stdin = sys.stdin.read() if "--input" in argv else ""
    70	spool = os.environ["MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_SPOOL"]
    71	with open(spool, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    72	    handle.write(json.dumps({"argv": argv, "method": method, "path": path,
    73	                             "rel": rel, "stdin": stdin}) + "\\n")
    74	
    75	with open(os.environ["MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_ROUTES"], encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    76	    routes = json.load(handle)
    77	state_path = spool + ".state"
    78	used = {}
    79	if os.path.exists(state_path):
    80	    with open(state_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    81	        used = json.load(handle)
    82	
    83	for index, rule in enumerate(routes):
    84	    key = str(index)
    85	    if rule.get("method", "GET") != method or not re.search(rule["path"], rel):
    86	        continue
    87	    if rule.get("once") and used.get(key):
    88	        continue
    89	    used[key] = used.get(key, 0) + 1
    90	    with open(state_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    91	        json.dump(used, handle)
    92	    if rule.get("fail"):
    93	        sys.stderr.write(rule.get("stderr") or "fake gh: canned refusal\\n")
    94	        raise SystemExit(1)
    95	    if "body" in rule:
    96	        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(rule["body"]))

   102	
   103	
   104	class FakeGitHub:
   105	    """A fake ``gh`` binary plus its route table, all inside one tempdir."""
   106	
   107	    def __init__(self, tmp: Path) -> None:
   108	        self.tmp = tmp
   109	        self.binary = tmp / "gh"
   110	        self.binary.write_text(FAKE_GH, encoding="utf-8")
   111	        self.binary.chmod(0o755)
   112	        self.spool = tmp / "gh-calls.jsonl"
   113	        self.routes_path = tmp / "gh-routes.json"
   114	        self.routes: list[dict] = []
   115	        self._flush()
   116	
   117	    def route(self, path: str, body=None, *, method: str = "GET",
   118	              fail: bool = False, once: bool = False) -> "FakeGitHub":
   119	        """Declare one reply.  *path* is a regex against the repo-relative route.
   120	
   121	        Rules match in declaration order, so a ``once=True`` rule in front of a
   122	        broader one models "state changed between two reads" — exactly the
   123	        adoption paths at ``gh_common.py:216-224`` and ``:336-343``.
   124	        """
   125	        rule: dict = {"path": path, "method": method}
   126	        if body is not None:
   127	            rule["body"] = body
   128	        if fail:
   129	            rule["fail"] = True
   130	        if once:
   131	            rule["once"] = True
   132	        self.routes.append(rule)
   133	        self._flush()
   134	        return self
   135	
   136	    def reset(self) -> None:
   137	        """Forget the routes and the call log; used between gate scenarios."""
   138	        self.routes = []
   139	        self._flush()
   140	        for path in (self.spool, Path(str(self.spool) + ".state")):
   141	            if path.exists():
   142	                path.unlink()
   143	
   144	    def env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
   145	        return {"MIPSTARRE_GH": str(self.binary),
   146	                "MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO": REPO,
   147	                "MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_SPOOL": str(self.spool),
   148	                "MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_ROUTES": str(self.routes_path)}
   149	
   150	    def calls(self) -> list[dict]:
   151	        if not self.spool.exists():
   152	            return []
   153	        return [json.loads(line) for line in
   154	                self.spool.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line]
   155	
   156	    def payloads(self, method: str, pattern: str) -> list[dict]:
   157	        """Decoded request bodies of the calls matching *method* and *pattern*."""
   158	        return [json.loads(call["stdin"]) for call in self.calls()
   159	                if call["method"] == method and re.search(pattern, call["rel"])
   160	                and call["stdin"]]
   161	
   162	    def _flush(self) -> None:
   163	        self.routes_path.write_text(json.dumps(self.routes), encoding="utf-8")
   164

   174	        patcher = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, self.gh.env())
   175	        patcher.start()

   415	#: A path segment into the archived registries.  The REST API also speaks
   416	#: ``issues/...``, so the two are told apart by what follows: a route always
   417	#: continues with an f-string field (``issues/{number}/comments``) or with
   418	#: ``comments/{id}`` (gh_common.py:213), while a tree reference continues with a
   419	#: literal id, glob or filename.
   420	_TREE_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.-])(?:issues|prs)/")
   421	_REST_ROUTE_RE = re.compile(r"^issues/(?:\{|comments/\{)")
   422	
   423	#: The other shape a tree reference takes: a join onto the repository root.
   424	_TREE_JOIN_RE = re.compile(
   425	    r"""(?:\$\{?ROOT\}?|\$\{?REPO_ROOT\}?|repo_root|REPO_ROOT)\s*/\s*["']?(?:issues|prs)\b""")

   428	def _active_source(path: Path) -> str:
   429	    """The file's live code: comments and docstrings blanked, line numbers kept.
   430	
   431	    Every surviving mention of the registries is historical narration ("Pre-0007
   432	    this wrote ``prs/<id>-<slug>/pr.md``", issue_new.py:2-5), so a grep over raw
   433	    text cannot express the rule.  Python comments come from ``tokenize`` (a
   434	    ``#`` inside a string is not a comment token) and docstrings from ``ast``;
   435	    shell keeps only its non-comment lines.
   436	    """
   437	    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   438	    if path.suffix == ".sh":
   439	        return "\n".join("" if line.lstrip().startswith("#") else line
   440	                         for line in text.splitlines())
   441	    lines = text.splitlines()
   442	    docstring_lines: set[int] = set()
   443	    for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(text)):
   444	        if isinstance(node, (ast.Module, ast.ClassDef, ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
   445	            if ast.get_docstring(node, clean=False) is not None:
   446	                first = node.body[0]

   727	    ledger.append("<!-- no findings -->")

   729	# review_state carries the verdict verbatim.  The lane file is runtime state,
   730	# not the record: what pr_merge.py reads is the published COMMENT review whose
   731	# body combine_review builds out of these two files.
   732	state = verdict
   733	job = "code-review" if kind == "code" else "prose-review"

   735	out = ["---",
   736	       "pr: %s" % pr,
   737	       "kind: %s" % kind,
   738	       "branch: %s" % branch,
   739	       "base: %s" % base,
   740	       "merge_base: %s" % merge_base,
   741	       "head_sha: %s" % head_sha,
   742	       "verdict: %s" % verdict,
   743	       "review_state: %s" % state,
   744	       "session: %s" % session,
   745	       "model: %s" % (model or "(dispatcher default)"),
   746	       "generated: %s" % generated,

   749	       "# %s review — PR %s @ %s" % (kind.capitalize(), pr, head_sha[:12]),
   750	       "",
   751	       "Local replacement for the `%s` job of `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`." % job,

   754	       "",
   755	       "Checkbox states: `[ ]` unresolved (blocks the merge), `[x]` resolved,",
   756	       "`[-]` outdated (the cited lines were rewritten; does not block).",
   757	       "",
   758	       "<!-- findings:begin -->"]

   761	            "",
   762	            "## Review",
   763	            "",
   764	            rest,
   765	            "",
   766	            "## Verdict",
   767	            "",
   768	            "VERDICT: %s" % verdict,

   772	                           prefix=".verdict-", suffix=".tmp")

   774	    fh.write("\n".join(out))

   778	print("unresolved=%d" % sum(1 for line in ledger if line.startswith("- [ ]")))
   779	PY
   780	}

   782	# ------------------------------------------------------- combined review body
   783	# combine_review <worst> <code-verdict> <prose-verdict> — fold the lane ledgers
   784	# into the ONE body published as the COMMENT review for this head SHA.  The
   785	# F-numbers are re-issued across both lanes so the merge gate counts unchecked
   786	# findings (^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]) over a single ledger, and the mandated line
   787	# "VERDICT: <state> (code=..., prose=...)" is emitted exactly once.
   788	# Prints "unresolved=N".
   789	combine_review() {
   790	  python3 - "$COMBINED_MD" "$CODE_MD" "$PROSE_MD" "$1" "$2" "$3" \
   791	    "$PR_NUM" "$HEAD_SHA" "$BRANCH" "$BASE" "$MERGE_BASE" "$(now_utc)" <<'PY'
   792	import os, re, sys, tempfile
   793	
   794	(dest, code_md, prose_md, worst, code_verdict, prose_verdict,
   795	 pr, head_sha, branch, base, merge_base, generated) = sys.argv[1:13]
   796	
   797	LEDGER = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*]\s*\[( |x|X|-)\]")
   798	NUMBER = re.compile(r"^(\s*[-*]\s*\[[ xX-]\]\s*)F\d+(\s*)")
   799	
   800	
   801	def lane(path):
   802	    """(ledger lines, prose body) of one lane file, or ([], "") when absent."""
   803	    if not path or not os.path.exists(path):
   804	        return [], ""
   805	    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
   806	    findings, keep = [], False
   807	    for line in text.split("\n"):
   808	        stripped = line.strip()
   809	        if stripped == "<!-- findings:begin -->":
   810	            keep = True
   811	            continue
   812	        if stripped == "<!-- findings:end -->":
   813	            keep = False
   814	            continue
   815	        if keep and LEDGER.match(line):
   816	            findings.append(line.rstrip())
   817	    body = text.split("\n## Review\n", 1)[-1].split("\n## Verdict\n", 1)[0]
   818	    return findings, body.strip("\n")
   819	
   820	
   821	code_findings, code_body = lane(code_md)
   822	# A prose file left by an earlier run at this SHA is ignored unless THIS run
   823	# produced a prose verdict: the cache outlives one review, the ledger must not.
   824	prose_findings, prose_body = lane(prose_md) if prose_verdict else ([], "")
   825	
   826	ledger, n = [], 0
   827	for tag, lines in (("code", code_findings), ("prose", prose_findings)):
   828	    for line in lines:
   829	        n += 1
   830	        renumbered = NUMBER.sub(lambda m: "%sF%d%s" % (m.group(1), n, m.group(2)), line, count=1)
   831	        ledger.append("%s  <!-- lane=%s -->" % (renumbered, tag))
   832	if not ledger:
   833	    ledger.append("<!-- no findings -->")
   834	
   835	out = ["# Review — PR %s @ %s" % (pr, head_sha[:12]),
   836	       "",
   837	       "VERDICT: %s (code=%s, prose=%s)" % (worst, code_verdict or "none",
   838	                                            prose_verdict or "n/a"),
   839	       "",
   840	       "Posted by `local/bin/review.sh` at %s — the local replacement for the "
   841	       "`code-review` and `prose-review` jobs of `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`."
   842	       % generated,
   843	       "",
   844	       "Branch `%s` onto `%s`; merge base `%s`; head `%s`." % (branch, base, merge_base, head_sha),
   845	       "",
   846	       "## Findings",
   847	       "",
   848	       "Checkbox states: `[ ]` unresolved (blocks the merge), `[x]` resolved.",
   849	       "Resolve a finding by ticking its box in this review body.",
   850	       "",
   851	       "<!-- findings:begin -->"]
   852	out.extend(ledger)
   853	out.extend(["<!-- findings:end -->", "", "## Code review", "", code_body or "(no body)"])
   854	if prose_verdict:
   855	    out.extend(["", "## Prose review", "", prose_body or "(no body)"])
   856	out.append("")
   857	
   858	fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=os.path.dirname(dest) or ".",
   859	                           prefix=".combined-", suffix=".tmp")
   860	with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
   861	    fh.write("\n".join(out))
   862	os.replace(tmp, dest)
   863	
   864	# The merge gate's own regex (local/protocols/issues-prs.md), applied to the
   865	# SAME text the gate will read — the whole combined body, not just the ledger —
   866	# so the status this script posts and pr_merge.py's count can never disagree
   867	# (a stray "- [ ]" bullet in a reviewer's prose counts for both or neither).
   868	UNCHECKED = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]", re.MULTILINE)
   869	print("unresolved=%d" % len(UNCHECKED.findall("\n".join(out))))
   870	PY
   871	}

   873	# --------------------------------------------------------------- code review
   874	CODE_PERSONA_PATH=".github/prompts/claude-code-review-system-prompt.md"
   875	CODE_TASK_PATH=".github/prompts/claude-code-review-prompt.md"
   876	fetch_trusted "$CODE_PERSONA_PATH" "$RUN_DIR/code-persona.md"
   877	fetch_trusted "$CODE_TASK_PATH" "$RUN_DIR/code-trusted-task.md"
   878	build_task code "$RUN_DIR/code-trusted-task.md" "$RUN_DIR/code-task.md"
   879	build_standalone "$RUN_DIR/code-persona.md" "$RUN_DIR/code-task.md" \
   880	  "$RUN_DIR/diff.sanitized.txt" "$RUN_DIR/code-standalone.md"
   881	
   882	PROSE_PERSONA_PATH=".github/prompts/blueprint-prose-review-system-prompt.md"
   883	PROSE_TASK_PATH=".github/prompts/blueprint-prose-review-prompt.md"
   884	if [ "$TOUCHES_BLUEPRINT" -eq 1 ]; then
   885	  fetch_trusted "$PROSE_PERSONA_PATH" "$RUN_DIR/prose-persona.md"
   886	  fetch_trusted "$PROSE_TASK_PATH" "$RUN_DIR/prose-trusted-task.md"
   887	  build_task prose "$RUN_DIR/prose-trusted-task.md" "$RUN_DIR/prose-task.md"
   888	  build_standalone "$RUN_DIR/prose-persona.md" "$RUN_DIR/prose-task.md" \
   889	    "$RUN_DIR/diff.sanitized.txt" "$RUN_DIR/prose-standalone.md"
   890	fi
   891	
   892	if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]; then
   893	  log "dry run; nothing was dispatched. Artefacts:"
   894	  log "  diff:         $RUN_DIR/diff.patch"
   895	  log "  code task:    $RUN_DIR/code-task.md"
   896	  log "  code fallback:$RUN_DIR/code-standalone.md"
   897	  if [ "$TOUCHES_BLUEPRINT" -eq 1 ]; then
   898	    log "  prose task:   $RUN_DIR/prose-task.md"

   901	  fi
   902	  log "  worktree:     $WORKTREE"
   903	  exit 0
   904	fi
   905	
   906	# The two review lanes are independent per head: dispatch them CONCURRENTLY
   907	# (EVOLUTION.md 2026-08-31, "Review lanes run in parallel").  Parsing stays
   908	# sequential below, and the failure semantics are unchanged: a code-lane
   909	# crash blocks the PR (and reaps the still-running prose lane); a prose-lane
   910	# failure only warns.
   911	log "running code review for PR $PR_NUM @ ${HEAD_SHA:0:12}"
   912	CODE_OUT="$RUN_DIR/code-last-message.md"
   913	rm -f "$CODE_OUT"
   914	CODE_RC_FILE="$RUN_DIR/code.rc"

   916	  run_agent reviewer read-only "$WORKTREE" "$CODE_PERSONA_PATH" \
   917	    "$RUN_DIR/code-task.md" "$RUN_DIR/code-standalone.md" \
   918	    "$RUN_DIR/diff.sanitized.txt" "$CODE_OUT" "$REVIEW_MODEL" || rc=$?

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	#
     3	# review.sh — model-backed review of a GitHub PR, chained after a green CI.
     4	#
     5	# Usage:
     6	#   local/bin/review.sh <pr-number> [--force-review] [--dry-run]
     7	#
     8	#   <pr-number>      GitHub PR number ("12").  Branch, base and head SHA come
     9	#                    from gh_common.py pr-view; the local branch tip must be
    10	#                    exactly the GitHub head before anything is reviewed.
    11	#   --force-review   Review even when the head commit is a bot fix commit.
    12	#                    Used by autofix.sh for the single forced review at the
    13	#                    iteration cap (local/protocols/autofix.md).
    14	#   --dry-run        Resolve the worktree, diff and prompts, print where they
    15	#                    landed, and stop before dispatching an agent.
    16	#
    17	# Local replacement for .github/workflows/pr-review.yml (gate + code-review +
    18	# prose-review jobs).  Protocol: local/protocols/review.md.
    19	#
    20	# GitHub is the record (gh_common.py:4-8).  The gate reads the local-ci/summary
    21	# commit status on the exact head SHA; the verdict is published as ONE COMMENT
    22	# review bound to that SHA plus a local-review/summary status.  Single-account
    23	# repos cannot self-APPROVE, so adverseness travels in the status, never in a
    24	# review state.  There is no local PR record: a GitHub failure fails this
    25	# script closed rather than leaving a fallback record behind.
    26	#
    27	# Exit codes:
    28	#   0  review published, or an intentional skip (kill switch, bot commit, stale
    29	#      head, empty diff)
    30	#   1  usage or environment error
    31	#   3  gate blocked: local-ci/summary is not success for the head SHA.  Nothing
    32	#      is published — the absence of a green local-review/summary is the block.
    33	#   4  the reviewer returned no machine-parseable verdict trailer.  A failing
    34	#      local-review/summary is posted so the PR never reads as green.
    35	#
    36	# Environment:
    37	#   LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED       disables the reviewer on the literal string
    38	#                              "false" only; unset means enabled.
    39	#   MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF      git ref the reviewer personas are read from
    40	#                              (default: main).  Never the branch under review.
    41	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL     codex model for the code review (default: the
    42	#                              dispatcher's / codex's own default)
    43	#   MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL      codex model for the blueprint prose review
    44	#                              (default: MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL)
    45	#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT        runtime state root (default ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev)
    46	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_LOCK_WAIT seconds to queue behind another review of the
    47	#                              same PR before giving up (default 1800)
    48	#   MIPSTARRE_DIFF_MAX_LINES   diff lines handed to the reviewer (default 4000)
    49	#   MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO      owner/repo override for gh_common.py
    50	#
    51	set -euo pipefail
    52	
    53	PROG="review.sh"
    54	BIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    55	SELF_ROOT="$(cd "$BIN_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    56	ROOT="$SELF_ROOT"
    57	# Worktrees are administered from the PRIMARY checkout: when this script runs
    58	# from a linked worktree copy, re-point the git root at the primary (same
    59	# resolution as cache-warmer.sh resolve_primary_repo; EVOLUTION.md 2026-08-30).
    60	# Only git operations follow the re-point — gh_common.py and the telemetry copy
    61	# stay in THIS checkout, which is also what wf_util.default_repo_root resolves
    62	# to (wf_util.py:46-48).
    63	_common="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null || true)"
    64	case "$_common" in
    65	  */.git) ROOT="$(dirname "$_common")" ;;
    66	esac
    67	unset _common
    68	
    69	# The one GitHub layer (gh_common.py:6-8); it ships beside this script.
    70	GH_COMMON="$BIN_DIR/gh_common.py"
    71	CACHE="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}"
    72	TRUSTED_REF="${MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF:-main}"
    73	DISPATCH="$ROOT/local/bin/dispatch.sh"
    74	REVIEW_MODEL="${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL:-}"

    77	DIFF_MAX_LINES="${MIPSTARRE_DIFF_MAX_LINES:-4000}"

    80	LOCK_HELD=""

    82	log()  { printf '%s: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2; }
    83	warn() { printf '%s: warning: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2; }
    84	die()  { printf '%s: error: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

    96	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- utilities

    98	now_utc() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

   100	# ghc <subcommand> ... — the only way this script talks to GitHub.  gh_common.py
   101	# exits 2 with the reason on stderr and never writes a local fallback record
   102	# (gh_common.py:19-20), so every caller here fails closed.
   103	ghc() { python3 "$GH_COMMON" "$@"; }

   105	# json_get <file> <dotted-path> — one scalar out of a gh_common JSON payload.
   106	# Absent keys print an empty line, so callers test with [ -n ... ] as they did
   107	# with the frontmatter reader this replaces.
   108	json_get() {
   109	  python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
   110	import json, sys
   111	try:
   112	    data = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
   113	except Exception as exc:
   114	    sys.stderr.write("review.sh: unreadable GitHub payload %s: %s\n" % (sys.argv[1], exc))
   115	    raise SystemExit(1)

   120	}

   122	# post_summary <state> <description> — the local-review/summary commit status on
   123	# the exact head SHA.  This status, not a review state, is what pr_merge.py
   124	# reads: an adverse verdict posts as a COMMENT review plus a failing status
   125	# (local/protocols/issues-prs.md).
   126	post_summary() {

   131	# sanitize_to <src> <dest> <max-lines> — control-char strip, fence breaking,
   132	# truncation (DESIGN.md invariant 6).  dispatch.sh sanitizes attachments again;
   133	# this is the copy that also protects the no-dispatcher fallback path.
   134	sanitize_to() {
   135	  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" <<'PY'
   136	import sys
   137	src, dest, max_lines = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
   138	try:
   139	    raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   140	except OSError:
   141	    raw = ""
   142	raw = raw.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
   143	keep = []
   144	for ch in raw:
   145	    o = ord(ch)
   146	    if ch in "\n\t" or (32 <= o < 127) or o > 159:
   147	        keep.append(ch)
   148	lines = "".join(keep).split("\n")
   149	truncated = 0
   150	if len(lines) > max_lines:
   151	    truncated = len(lines) - max_lines
   152	    lines = lines[:max_lines]
   153	out = []
   154	for line in lines:
   155	    line = line.replace("```", "'''").replace("~~~", "'''")
   156	    if line.startswith("<<<") or line.startswith("# Task"):
   157	        line = " " + line
   158	    out.append(line)
   159	if truncated:
   160	    out.append("... [%d further lines omitted by review.sh; full text on disk]"
   161	               % truncated)
   162	open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out) + "\n")
   163	PY
   164	}

   166	# acquire_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
   167	# Per-PR review lock.  No cancellation: a queued review waits and then
   168	# re-checks the head SHA (pr-review.yml:18-20, cancel-in-progress false).
   169	acquire_lock() {
   170	  local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 holder=""
   171	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
   172	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   173	    holder="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   174	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
   175	      warn "removing stale lock $dir (holder pid $holder is gone)"
   176	      rm -rf "$dir"
   177	      continue
   178	    fi
   179	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   180	      die "timed out after ${wait_s}s waiting for the review lock $dir (holder pid ${holder:-unknown})"
   181	    fi
   182	    [ "$waited" = 0 ] && log "another review holds $dir (pid ${holder:-unknown}); queuing"
   183	    sleep 5
   184	    waited=$((waited + 5))
   185	  done
   186	  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   187	  printf '%s\n' "$label" >"$dir/label"
   188	  LOCK_HELD="$dir"
   189	}

   485	# ledgers land next to it as <sha>-{code,prose,combined}.md.

   234	## 9. The findings ledger
   235	
   236	`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
   237	review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
   238	`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
   239	`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
   240	GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
   241	status signal; the REST `line` field lied.
   242	
   243	Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
   244	`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
   245	`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:
   246	
   247	    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis
   248	
   249	| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
   250	|---|---|---|
   251	| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
   252	| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
   253	| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |
   254	
   255	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   256	expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
   257	pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
   258	that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
   259	nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
   260	disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.
   261	
   262	**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
   263	not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
   264	unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
   265	the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
   266	clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
   267	must be resolved, outdated, or explicitly overridden by the user — and per
   268	`docs/pr_review_management.md`, "never merge without user consent" is the
   269	standing rule that override is *not* the automation's to exercise.
   270	
   271	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   272	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   273	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
   274	all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
   275	next review re-derives from the new diff.
   276	
   277	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
   278	`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
   279	directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
   280	merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
   281	silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
   282	finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.
   283	
   284	## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`
   285	
   286	`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
   287	`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;
   288	`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR
   289	proliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on
   290	branch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name
   291	validation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming
   292	(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).
   293	
   294	The local translation is:
   295	
   296	| Parent | Local | Who starts it |
   297	|---|---|---|
   298	| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   299	| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   300	| auto-fix workflows | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode ...` | CI/review chain or a human |
   301	
   302	`agent.sh` is **never invoked by automation.**  `claude.yml:24-30` gated the
   303	responder on `sender.type != 'Bot'` because a bot echoing `@claude` into a
   304	comment would start a write-enabled, secret-bearing session; the local form is
   305	that `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` export `MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1` (and
   306	`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1`) around every agent they run, and `agent.sh`
   307	refuses to start when either is set.  `agent.sh` also refuses while a fix lock
   308	is held for its branch: two writers on one branch is the parallel-push
   309	collision that `auto-fix.yml:253-256` serialised away.

   311	The author_association gate has no local analogue and is dropped — the human
   312	running the command *is* the authorisation.  The `]`-in-branch-name lesson
   313	survives as a lint in all three scripts.

   315	`agent.sh` may commit; it must not use the `[codex-auto-fix]` /
   316	`[codex-review-fix]` prefixes, because a human-directed commit must be
   317	reviewable and those prefixes make the reviewer skip.  The script warns if the
   318	session used one anyway.

   320	The auto-create-PR step of `claude.yml` becomes a printed instruction rather
   321	than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
   322	tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
   323	branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).

   325	## 11. Operating it
   326	
   327	    local/bin/review.sh 7                # review PR 0007 at its current head
   328	    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
   329	    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch
   330	
   331	Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
   332	`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
   333	Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
   334	the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
   335	neither publishes a review.
   336	
   337	Artefacts:
   338	
   339	| Path | Committed | Contents |
   340	|---|---|---|
   341	| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
   342	| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
   343	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
   344	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |
   345	
   346	Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so
   347	the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
   348	summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
   349	(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
   350	back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
   351	in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
   352	is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
   353	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
   354	agreeing is intentional redundancy.
   355	
   356	Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
   357	block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
   358	hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
   359	not a verdict.

   361	## 12. Deliberately not ported
   362	
   363	* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
   364	  One reviewer session; the cascade
   365	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS > CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER > anthropic` becomes
   366	  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
   367	* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
   368	  comes from a branch of this single repository.
   369	* **Thread resolution via `mcp__github__resolve_review_thread`.**  Replaced by
   370	  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.
   371	* **`allowed-tools` presets and `allowed-tools.json`.**  codex sandbox modes
   372	  (`read-only` for review, `workspace-write` for fixes) carry the same intent
   373	  with a coarser grain: read-only genuinely prevents writes, which the
   374	  allow-list only approximated.
   375	* **`id-token`/OAuth plumbing, `LionSR/agent-ci-actions`, plugin marketplaces.**
   376	  Local codex configuration replaces them (`.codex/`, `local/protocols/sessions.md`).

   379	## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)
   380	
   381	A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
   382	the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:
   383	
   384	1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   385	   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   386	   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   387	   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   388	   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   389	   `moot: <reason>`);
   390	2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
   391	3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
   392	4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   393	   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.
   394	
   395	Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
   396	This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
   397	terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.

390	# The reviewer reads the local worktree, so the local tip and the GitHub head
   391	# must be the same commit before anything is dispatched: a verdict bound to the
   392	# GitHub head that describes different local bytes is worse than no verdict.

   404	# manifest is consulted, and no fallback is invented when GitHub is unreachable.

     3	
     4	The one script in the issue-lifecycle area that changes ``main``: the local
     5	replacement for GitHub's branch-protection rules, which upstream were server-side
     6	settings no client could bypass.  A single-account repository has none — the owner can
     7	always press Merge — so the authority is this file.  It refuses by default, every
     8	override is named, and ``gh_common.merge_pr`` merges through the REST ``sha`` guard,
     9	which makes GitHub reject the call if the head moved meanwhile.
    10	
    11	Every piece of evidence lives on GitHub, bound to the head SHA (issues-prs.md; the old
    12	``prs/`` registry is archived under ``results/telemetry/registry-archive/``):
    13	
    14	1. the PR is open, unmerged, not a draft;
    15	2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip is that
    16	   SHA — the merge must be of the bytes that were built here;
    17	3. the eight ``local-ci/<step>`` contexts (ci.sh:70) and ``local-ci/summary`` are
    18	   ``success`` on it.  A missing context blocks: GitHub's combined state reads
    19	   "success" for a commit carrying no statuses at all;

    21	   commit id, its ``VERDICT:`` line is APPROVED (or COMMENTED with zero unchecked
    22	   findings), and ``local-review/summary`` is ``success`` (DESIGN.md:66-69) — one
