   232	rewritten under it.
   233	
   234	## 9. The findings ledger
   235	
   236	`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
   237	review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
   238	`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
   239	`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
   240	GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
   241	status signal; the REST `line` field lied.
   242	
   243	Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
   244	`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
   245	`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:
   246	
   247	    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis
   248	
   249	| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
   250	|---|---|---|
   251	| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
   252	| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
   253	| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |
   254	
   255	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   256	expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
   257	pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
   258	that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
   259	nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
   260	disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.
   261	
   262	**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
   263	not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
   264	unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
   265	the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
   266	clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
   267	must be resolved, outdated, or explicitly overridden by the user — and per
   268	`docs/pr_review_management.md`, "never merge without user consent" is the
   269	standing rule that override is *not* the automation's to exercise.
   270	
   271	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   272	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   273	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
   274	all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
   275	next review re-derives from the new diff.
   276	
   277	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
   278	`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
   279	directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
   280	merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
   281	silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
   282	finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.
   283	
   284	## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`
   285	
   286	`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
   287	`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;
   288	`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR
   289	proliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on
   290	branch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name
   291	validation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming
   292	(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).
   293	
   294	The local translation is:
   295	
   296	| Parent | Local | Who starts it |
   297	|---|---|---|
   298	| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   299	| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   300	| auto-fix workflows | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode ...` | CI/review chain or a human |
   301	
   302	`agent.sh` is **never invoked by automation.**  `claude.yml:24-30` gated the
   303	responder on `sender.type != 'Bot'` because a bot echoing `@claude` into a
   304	comment would start a write-enabled, secret-bearing session; the local form is
   305	that `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` export `MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1` (and
   306	`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1`) around every agent they run, and `agent.sh`
   307	refuses to start when either is set.  `agent.sh` also refuses while a fix lock
   308	is held for its branch: two writers on one branch is the parallel-push
   309	collision that `auto-fix.yml:253-256` serialised away.
   310	
   311	The author_association gate has no local analogue and is dropped — the human
   312	running the command *is* the authorisation.  The `]`-in-branch-name lesson
   313	survives as a lint in all three scripts.
   314	
   315	`agent.sh` may commit; it must not use the `[codex-auto-fix]` /
   316	`[codex-review-fix]` prefixes, because a human-directed commit must be
   317	reviewable and those prefixes make the reviewer skip.  The script warns if the
   318	session used one anyway.
   319	
   320	The auto-create-PR step of `claude.yml` becomes a printed instruction rather
   321	than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
   322	tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
   323	branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).
   324	
   325	## 11. Operating it
   326	
   327	    local/bin/review.sh 7                # review PR 0007 at its current head
   328	    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
   329	    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch
   330	
   331	Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
   332	`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
   333	Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
   334	the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
   335	neither publishes a review.
   336	
   337	Artefacts:
   338	
   339	| Path | Committed | Contents |
   340	|---|---|---|
   341	| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
   342	| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
   343	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
   344	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |
   345	
   346	Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so
   347	the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
   348	summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
   349	(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
   350	back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
   351	in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
   352	is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
   353	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
   354	agreeing is intentional redundancy.
   355	
   356	Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
   357	block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
   358	hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
   359	not a verdict.

   361	## 12. Deliberately not ported
   362	
   363	* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
   364	  One reviewer session; the cascade
   365	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS > CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER > anthropic` becomes
   366	  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
   367	* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
   368	  comes from a branch of this single repository.
   369	* **Thread resolution via `mcp__github__resolve_review_thread`.**  Replaced by
   370	  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.
     1	# Agent sessions — naming, dispatch, verification, archival
     2	
     3	Normative. Read `local/protocols/meta.md` first.
     4	
     5	A *session* is one `codex exec` run: a single model conversation with a
     6	working root, a sandbox mode, a persona, a task, and a token bill. In the
     7	parent repository a session was a GitHub Actions job — its identity came from
     8	a bot token, its prompt from a trusted checkout of the default branch, and its
     9	accounting from the Actions API (`.github/workflows/claude.yml`,
    10	`pr-review.yml`, `auto-fix.yml`). None of those three services exist locally,
    11	so this protocol reconstructs each one explicitly:
    12	
    13	| GitHub-era service | Local reconstruction |
    14	|---|---|
    15	| bot identity (`BOT_PAT`, `claude[bot]`) | the session name and `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` |
    16	| trusted prompt checkout (`.trusted-actions/`, default branch) | `git show main:<persona>` inside `dispatch.sh` |
    17	| run accounting (Actions API, run ids, job logs) | the captured `--json` event stream + `telemetry.py` |
    18	| `@claude` / `@codex` mention trigger with an `author_association` gate | the human or orchestrator who runs `dispatch.sh` |
    19	| Codex-cloud environment hooks (`.codex/setup.sh`, `.codex/maintenance.sh`) | `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`, run before dispatch |
    20	| agent-runtime "pinned memories" (`AGENTS.md:658`) | the registry plus the archived capture files |
    21	
    22	## 1. One entry point
    23	
    24	**Every session is started by `local/bin/dispatch.sh`.** Calling `codex` by
    25	hand — including from inside an agent session — is a protocol violation, not a
    26	shortcut: the thread id, the token counts and the wall time exist only in the
    27	event stream that `dispatch.sh` captures, and a session started any other way
    28	is invisible to the study. `meta.md` permits exactly one repair: backfill a
    29	registry line with `dispatcher: manual`, and log why in
    30	`results/telemetry/events.md`.
    31	
    32	This rule is inherited, not invented. The parent repository refused to start
    33	an agent from an untrusted trigger for the same structural reason — a runner
    34	with write permissions and secrets must have a single, gated entry
    35	(`claude.yml:24-30`: "this workflow runs with write permissions and repo
    36	secrets, so prompt-injection from untrusted commenters must not start the
    37	runner"). Locally the secrets are gone but the write access is not.
    38	
    39	An agent that needs a sub-session (an orchestrator splitting work, a prover
    40	asking for a scout) invokes `dispatch.sh` from inside its own session, with
    41	`MIPSTARRE_SESSION` set to its own name so the registry records the parent in
    42	the `dispatcher` field. The session prompt states this rule verbatim.
    43	
    44	## 2. Roles and sandboxes
    45	
    46	Seven roles, fixed (`DESIGN.md`, "Naming and identity conventions"):
    47	
    48	`orc`, `prover`, `reviewer`, `simplifier`, `blueprint`, `splitter`, `scout`.
    49	
    50	Sandbox defaults follow from what the role is allowed to change:
    51	
    52	| Role | Default sandbox | Rationale |
    53	|---|---|---|
    54	| `reviewer`, `scout` | `read-only` | a reader must not be able to edit what it reports on |
    55	| all others | `workspace-write` | they exist to change the worktree |
    56	
    57	`--sandbox` overrides the default; asking for a writable reviewer produces a
    58	loud warning, because a reviewer that can fix what it found has reviewed its
    59	own diff (§6). `danger-full-access` disables the codex sandbox entirely and
    60	warns; it is never a default.
    61	
    62	The persona for a role lives at `local/personas/<role>.md`, with one naming
    63	exception: the role code `orc` maps to `local/personas/orchestrator.md`.
    64	Until such a file is committed, `dispatch.sh` warns and falls back to a
    65	one-line built-in frame — enough to run, not enough for load-bearing work.
    66	
    67	## 3. Naming
    68	
    69	```
    70	<role>-<scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq>        e.g. prover-0042-20260830-01
    71	```
    72	
    73	- `scope` is the `--issue` argument normalized to `[a-z0-9-]`, at most 40
    74	  characters. An argument containing any of `[ ] ~ ^ : ? * \` is **rejected**,
    75	  not sanitized. This is the bracket-free naming invariant
    76	  (`DESIGN.md` invariant 9): the parent repository traced a class of automation
    77	  failures to `]` surviving from bracketed issue titles into generated branch
    78	  names, and adopted the convention as the fix
    79	  (`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).
    80	  Rejecting rather than stripping keeps the session name, the branch name and
    81	  the issue id referring to the same string.
    82	- `seq` is a two-digit counter, allocated under
    83	  `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/session-seq.lock` by scanning *both*
    84	  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` and `results/telemetry/sessions/` — a
    85	  session that crashed before its registry line was written still owns its
    86	  number, because its capture file exists.
    87	- Names are stable identifiers: they appear in the registry, in capture file
    88	  names, in the `dispatcher` field of child sessions, and in `audits/` reports.
    89	  Never reuse one.
    90	
    91	## 4. Lifecycle
    92	
    93	### 4.1 Dispatch
    94	
    95	```bash
    96	local/bin/dispatch.sh --role prover --issue 0042 \
    97	  --worktree .worktrees/issue-0042-pauli-basis \
    98	  --effort high \
    99	  -- "Close the sorry at MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean:212 ..."
   100	```
   101	
   102	`dispatch.sh` performs, in order: role and scope validation; kill-switch check
   103	(§9); session-name allocation; git-hook installation and verification in the
   104	worktree; persona read from the trusted ref; prompt composition; the codex run
   105	with the event stream teed to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`;
   106	registry append; and a final report of `name`, `thread_id` and the
   107	last-message path.
   108	
   109	Preconditions the dispatcher (human or orchestrator) owns:
   110	
   111	1. The worktree exists and has been prepared by `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`.
   112	   `dispatch.sh` creates no worktrees and fetches no caches; it fails with a
   113	   message naming the setup script.
   114	2. The git hooks are installed there. `dispatch.sh` installs and verifies them
   115	   for every writing session, because `core.hooksPath` is per-worktree and a
   116	   fresh worktree starts unprotected. Locally there is no CI backstop, so the
   117	   hooks are the only gate that catches statement drift before it is committed
   118	   (`AGENTS.md:83-85`).
   119	3. The task prompt is self-contained. A dispatched session cannot see the
   120	   dispatcher's conversation; write to it as to a colleague who was not in the
   121	   room, citing files, blueprint labels and theorem names rather than "the
   122	   thing we discussed".
   123	
   124	Data the session should read but not obey — build logs, review findings, issue
   125	bodies — is attached with `--context-file`, never pasted into the task text
   126	(§7).
   127	
   128	### 4.2 Work
   129	
   130	The session works in its worktree under its sandbox. The standing rules
   131	injected into every prompt are: read `AGENTS.md` first; treat
   132	`local/protocols/*.md` as normative; start no sub-session except through
   133	`dispatch.sh`; never review your own diff; keep runtime state out of the
   134	repository; and put the result, the residual risk and the hand-off in the
   135	final message, which is captured to
   136	`results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.last.md`.
   137	
   138	### 4.3 Verify
   139	
   140	A session is not finished when the model stops. Before its work is accepted:
   141	
   142	1. the validation ladder from `AGENTS.md` has been run (single-file
   143	   `lake env lean` checks, then the `sorry`/`axiom` scan, then `lake build`);
   144	2. the hooks pass — a failing `pre-push` is the local equivalent of a red CI
   145	   and keeps the branch unmerged;
   146	3. for Lean or blueprint changes, a **different** session has reviewed the
   147	   diff (§6);
   148	4. the final message exists and says what was done, what was not, and what the
   149	   next session needs. An empty `<name>.last.md` is reported as a warning by
   150	   `dispatch.sh` and should be treated as an incomplete session.
   151	
   152	Verification failures are not silent. A failed codex run is recorded with
   153	`status: failed` and its exit code, and `dispatch.sh` exits with that code —
   154	the same fail-loudly semantics the parent repository adopted after a skipped
   155	review read as green (`pr-review.yml:59-60`: "PR Review must not report
   156	success without a review").
   157	
   158	### 4.4 Archive
   159	
   160	Archiving a session means three things, in this order:
   161	
   162	```bash
   163	# 1. the record: append a superseding status line
   164	python3 local/bin/telemetry.py session-status \
   165	  --name prover-0042-20260830-01 --status archived \
   166	  --note "merged as <sha>; residual sorry tracked in GitHub issue #43"
   167	
   168	# 2. the worktree: remove it once nothing depends on it
   169	git worktree remove .worktrees/issue-0042-pauli-basis
   170	
   171	# 3. the lesson (only when there is one)
   172	python3 local/bin/telemetry.py event --text "…symptom → diagnosis → fix → lesson"
   173	```
   174	
   175	**The JSONL capture is the archive.** `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`
   176	and `<name>.last.md` are committed and never rewritten; the worktree is
   177	disposable and the codex rollout under `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/` is
   178	outside the repository and outside our control. The registry line records the
   179	resolved rollout path when one is found, because the store is date-sharded and
   180	a bare thread id is not enough to locate it later.
     1	# Meta-protocol — how this workflow evolves
     2	
     3	Read this before any other protocol. It governs how the protocols themselves
     4	change, and the telemetry duties that make the project usable as research data.
     5	
     6	## Standing principles
     7	
     8	1. **Protocols are normative until amended.** An agent that finds a protocol
     9	   wrong, ambiguous, or costly does not silently deviate: it follows the
    10	   protocol (or stops), records the friction in
    11	   `results/telemetry/events.md`, and proposes an amendment.
    12	2. **Amendments are evidence-driven.** Every change to a file under
    13	   `local/protocols/` or to `AGENTS.md` must append an entry to
    14	   `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` citing its trigger: an `events.md` incident,
    15	   a telemetry observation (e.g. repeated duplicate builds in
    16	   `builds.jsonl`), or an upstream policy decision by the user. No trigger,
    17	   no amendment.
    18	3. **The parent repo is precedent, not law.** The GitHub-era mechanism (frozen
    19	   under `.github/`, mapped in `local/DESIGN.md`) is the default answer to
    20	   "how should this work?"; deviations are fine when the local setting
    21	   genuinely differs, and must be recorded in `EVOLUTION.md` with the reason.
    22	4. **De-automation is a valid evolution step.** The parent workflow repeatedly
    23	   demoted LLM agents to deterministic scripts once the mechanical half of a
    24	   job was understood (issue-automation.yml:13-21), and demoted CI jobs to
    25	   notices when resources were exhausted. Prefer the cheapest mechanism that
    26	   holds the invariant.
    27	5. **Two memory disciplines.** Reports and session records are append-only and
    28	   never rewritten (supersede with dated status notes). Protocol documents
    29	   and paper-gap notes are living documents that are rewritten in place
    30	   (history lives in git and `EVOLUTION.md`). Do not mix the two.
    31	
    32	## Amendment procedure
    33	
    34	1. Write the incident/observation in `results/telemetry/events.md` (dated).
    35	2. Draft the protocol edit.
    36	3. Append to `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`:
    37	   `## YYYY-MM-DD — <short title>` with fields **Trigger** (cite events.md
    38	   entry or telemetry line), **Change** (files + gist), **Expected effect**,
    39	   and, when known later, **Outcome**.
    40	4. Commit protocol edit and ledger entry together, `docs(local)` scope.
    41	5. If the change alters guard semantics (locks, caps, gates, kill switches),
    42	   grep `local/` for every enforcement point and update all of them in the
    43	   same commit — the parent repo maintained such consistency invariants
    44	   through cross-referencing comments; we inherit the same drift risk.
    45	
    46	## Telemetry duties
    47	
    48	Schemas (all JSONL, one object per line; timestamps ISO-8601 with offset):
    49	
    50	- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` —
    51	  `{ts, stage, event: start|end|milestone, note?, tokens_note?}`
    52	  Stages: `1-skeleton`, `2-references`, `3-blueprint`, `4.1-minimal`,
    53	  `4.2-full-skeleton`, `4.3-proofs` (extend as needed).
    54	- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` —
    55	  `{name, role, issue, pr?, thread_id, start, end, wall_s,
    56	    usage: {input, cached_input, cache_write, output, reasoning},
    57	    exit, dispatcher, worktree, status: active|done|failed|archived}`
    58	  Written only by `local/bin/dispatch.sh` / `telemetry.py`.
    59	- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` —
    60	  `{ts, kind: warm|rebuild|cache-get|ci-build, trigger, seconds, outcome,
    61	    sha?, note?}`
    62	- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated bullets; free prose; one incident per
    63	  bullet: symptom → diagnosis → fix → lesson.
    64	
    65	Duties:
    66	
    67	- **Every agent session goes through `dispatch.sh`** so token usage and wall
    68	  time land in `sessions.jsonl`. A session started any other way is a
    69	  telemetry hole; if one happens, backfill a line with `dispatcher: manual`.
    70	- **Every full build** (warmer, CI, cold rebuild) lands in `builds.jsonl`.
    71	- **Stage transitions** are logged by the orchestrator (main session) at the
    72	  moment they happen, not reconstructed later.
    73	- Claude-side (non-codex) subagent fleets are summarized into `stages.jsonl`
    74	  as `milestone` entries with token totals, since they bypass `dispatch.sh`.
    75	
    76	## Research-data invariants
    77	
    78	The project doubles as a study of a self-evolving formalization workflow.
    79	Three artifacts must therefore stay trustworthy:
    80	
    81	- `EVOLUTION.md` — complete: every protocol change has an entry.
    82	- `events.md` — honest: failures are recorded as failures, including agent
    83	  mistakes, wasted builds, and reverted work.
    84	- `sessions.jsonl` + `stages.jsonl` — quantitative: per-stage cost
    85	  (time, tokens, session counts) reconstructible by a script, not by memory.

45	All evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).
    46	
    47	**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one
    48	`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,
    49	`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,
    50	`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.
    51	`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`
    52	after it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads
    53	the *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined
    54	status, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one
    55	PR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by
    56	`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.
    57	
    58	**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,
    59	carrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the
    60	line `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.
    61	Unchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`; clean means
    62	`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`
    63	too — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review
    64	event carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`
    65	(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.
    66	
    67	**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with
    68	`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition
    69	line per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.
    70	
    71	**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated
    72	read finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating
    73	it (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than
    74	webhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.
    75	
    76	## 3. The merge gate
    77	
    78	`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,
    79	never push `main`. The merge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact
    80	`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge
    81	commit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates
    82	that refuse by default:
    83	
    84	1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely
    85	   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;
    86	2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip
    87	   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here;
    88	3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on
    89	   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state
    90	   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;
    91	4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or
    92	   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is
    93	   `success` there;
    94	5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;
    95	6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder),
    96	   and the fix-iteration count — `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts
    97	   with a §1 fix prefix — is within `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP`;
    98	7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not
    99	   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.
   100	
   101	`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when
   102	an exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.
   103	
   104	Afterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the
   105	remote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local
   106	dirt defers it with a warning).
   107	
   108	## 4. Untrusted text
   109	
   110	Issue and PR bodies are untrusted data, and **more** so now that they arrive
   150	
   151	A single account cannot approve its own pull request, so GitHub's review-state
   152	field carries no authority here (`issues-prs.md` §2): the verdict is a trailer
   153	in the agent's last message (`codex exec -o <file>`), and the contract demands
   154	three things in order:
   155	
   156	1. a `## Findings` section, one line per finding, in exactly this shape:
   157	
   158	       - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Path/File.lean:123` — one-line summary
   159	
   160	   with severity in {`blocker`, `changes`, `advisory`} and `-` in place of
   161	   `path:line` when a finding is not tied to a line; or the single line
   162	   `- none`;
   163	2. a `## Review` section with the prose;
   164	3. as the final line, alone:
   165	
   166	       VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED
   167	
   168	A missing or malformed trailer is **not** an approval: `review.sh` exits 4,
   169	posts a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and keeps the raw output under
   170	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/`.  Nothing in the findings section
   171	is discarded either — a line that does not parse is kept verbatim as a
   172	`changes`-severity finding labelled `unparsed finding:`, and a non-approving
   173	verdict with an empty ledger gets one synthesised finding so the merge gate
   174	still blocks.  Both rules follow the same principle as rung 5: the failure mode
   175	worth engineering against is a review that reads green without having happened.
   176	
   177	## 7. Which reviews run
   178	
   179	* **Code review** always.  `pr-review.yml` ran it as a matrix over
   180	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` (anthropic, deepseek).  Locally the matrix
   181	  collapses to one codex session; a second backend can be added by running
   182	  `review.sh` again with `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL` set, which writes a separate
   183	  per-SHA file only if you also change the file name, so treat multi-provider
   184	  review as unimplemented rather than as a one-liner.
   185	* **Prose review** only when the diff touches `blueprint/`.  On GitHub it ran
   186	  unconditionally on a cheaper tier; gating it on the diff is a local
   187	  cost decision, not a weakening — the prose prompt reviews blueprint ↔ Lean
   188	  equivalence and blueprint prose, and a diff that touches no blueprint file
   189	  has nothing for it to review.  Set `MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL` for the
   190	  cheaper-tier split.
   191	
   192	The failure semantics of the two are deliberately different, and the difference
   193	is inherited: `pr-review.yml:112-131` *fails* the code review when its token is
   194	missing, while `pr-review.yml:202-224` *skips* the prose review in the same
   195	situation.  Locally, a code reviewer that dies without output blocks the PR; a
   196	prose reviewer that dies leaves a warning and the code verdict stands.
   197	
   198	The published verdict takes the **worst** of the two lanes, written verbatim on
   199	the `VERDICT:` line of one exact-head `COMMENT` review (marker
   200	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`): `APPROVED`, `COMMENTED` or
   201	`CHANGES_REQUESTED`.  Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT` too; adverseness lives
   202	in the paired `local-review/summary` status, `success` only for `APPROVED` or a
   203	`COMMENTED` verdict with an empty ledger and `failure` otherwise.  A head with
   204	no review at all simply has no such status, which the merge gate reads as
   205	"not reviewed" rather than as a pass.
   206

     8	they were file writes; now they are ``gh api`` calls, so the suite pins them by
     9	standing a fake ``gh`` in front of the layer.

    11	The fake is a small Python script this file writes into a tempdir and points
    12	``MIPSTARRE_GH`` at (the override read at ``gh_common.py:57-67``).  It logs
    13	argv+stdin to a spool and answers from a canned route table, so every test here
    14	runs offline, needs no ``gh`` installed, and asserts on the *wire* contract —
    15	the route, the method and the JSON payload — rather than on a mock's call list.
    16	An unmatched route fails the call: a test that forgets to declare one sees it.

    18	Coverage mirrors the layer's failure modes, one test each: status reduction and
    19	posting, comment/review idempotency and post-failure adoption, the merge
    20	topology check, label validation and key-marker adoption, the ``pr_merge.py``
    21	gate ladder (fail-closed on missing CI evidence and on an adverse verdict), the
    22	audit snapshot, and a hygiene check that no live tool still reaches for the
    23	retired registry trees.

    58	FAKE_GH = '''#!/usr/bin/env python3
    59	"""Stand-in for the gh CLI: log every call, answer from a canned route table."""
    60	import json
    61	import os
    62	import re
    63	import sys
    64	
    65	argv = sys.argv[1:]
    66	method = argv[argv.index("-X") + 1] if "-X" in argv else "GET"
    67	path = argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else ""
    68	rel = re.sub(r"^repos/[^/]+/[^/]+/", "", path)
    69	stdin = sys.stdin.read() if "--input" in argv else ""
    70	spool = os.environ["MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_SPOOL"]
    71	with open(spool, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    72	    handle.write(json.dumps({"argv": argv, "method": method, "path": path,
    73	                             "rel": rel, "stdin": stdin}) + "\\n")
    74	
    75	with open(os.environ["MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_ROUTES"], encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    76	    routes = json.load(handle)
    77	state_path = spool + ".state"
    78	used = {}
    79	if os.path.exists(state_path):
    80	    with open(state_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    81	        used = json.load(handle)
    82	
    83	for index, rule in enumerate(routes):
    84	    key = str(index)
    85	    if rule.get("method", "GET") != method or not re.search(rule["path"], rel):
    86	        continue
    87	    if rule.get("once") and used.get(key):
    88	        continue
    89	    used[key] = used.get(key, 0) + 1
    90	    with open(state_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    91	        json.dump(used, handle)
    92	    if rule.get("fail"):
    93	        sys.stderr.write(rule.get("stderr") or "fake gh: canned refusal\\n")
    94	        raise SystemExit(1)
    95	    if "body" in rule:
    96	        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(rule["body"]))
    97	    raise SystemExit(0)
    98	
    99	sys.stderr.write("fake gh: no route for %s %s\\n" % (method, rel))
   100	raise SystemExit(1)
   101	'''

   103	
   104	class FakeGitHub:
   105	    """A fake ``gh`` binary plus its route table, all inside one tempdir."""
   106	
   107	    def __init__(self, tmp: Path) -> None:
   108	        self.tmp = tmp
   109	        self.binary = tmp / "gh"
   110	        self.binary.write_text(FAKE_GH, encoding="utf-8")
   111	        self.binary.chmod(0o755)
   112	        self.spool = tmp / "gh-calls.jsonl"
   113	        self.routes_path = tmp / "gh-routes.json"
   114	        self.routes: list[dict] = []
   115	        self._flush()
   116	
   117	    def route(self, path: str, body=None, *, method: str = "GET",
   118	              fail: bool = False, once: bool = False) -> "FakeGitHub":
   119	        """Declare one reply.  *path* is a regex against the repo-relative route.
   120	
   121	        Rules match in declaration order, so a ``once=True`` rule in front of a
   122	        broader one models "state changed between two reads" — exactly the
   123	        adoption paths at ``gh_common.py:216-224`` and ``:336-343``.
   124	        """
   125	        rule: dict = {"path": path, "method": method}
   126	        if body is not None:
   127	            rule["body"] = body
   128	        if fail:
   129	            rule["fail"] = True
   130	        if once:
   131	            rule["once"] = True
   132	        self.routes.append(rule)
   133	        self._flush()
   134	        return self
   135	
   136	    def reset(self) -> None:
   137	        """Forget the routes and the call log; used between gate scenarios."""
   138	        self.routes = []
   139	        self._flush()
   140	        for path in (self.spool, Path(str(self.spool) + ".state")):
   141	            if path.exists():
   142	                path.unlink()
   143	
   144	    def env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
   145	        return {"MIPSTARRE_GH": str(self.binary),
   146	                "MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO": REPO,
   147	                "MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_SPOOL": str(self.spool),
   148	                "MIPSTARRE_FAKE_GH_ROUTES": str(self.routes_path)}
   149	
   150	    def calls(self) -> list[dict]:
   151	        if not self.spool.exists():
   152	            return []
   153	        return [json.loads(line) for line in
   154	                self.spool.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line]
   155	
   156	    def payloads(self, method: str, pattern: str) -> list[dict]:
   157	        """Decoded request bodies of the calls matching *method* and *pattern*."""
   158	        return [json.loads(call["stdin"]) for call in self.calls()
   159	                if call["method"] == method and re.search(pattern, call["rel"])
   160	                and call["stdin"]]
   161	
   162	    def _flush(self) -> None:
   163	        self.routes_path.write_text(json.dumps(self.routes), encoding="utf-8")

+# Brief: GitHub-native records with a durable local fallback
+
+Issue: `#0007`
+Target branch: `issue-0007-github-native-workflow`
+Expected PR title: `feat(local): add GitHub write-through records`
+
+## Objective
+
+Implement the 2026-08-31 owner decision recorded in `HANDOFF.md` step 0 and
+`local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`: GitHub becomes the ordinary issue and pull
+request surface for `Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`, while the existing committed
+registry remains a complete write-through record and an offline fallback.
+
+Local CI and review continue to execute on this server. The local same-head
+manifest, verdict, and merge gate remain authoritative. The GitHub adapter
+publishes those results; it must not weaken, duplicate, or replace the gate.
+
+This is workflow work only. Do not modify Lean, blueprint, or paper-source
+content.
+
+## Sources to read first
+
+1. `HANDOFF.md`, especially immediate step 0.
+2. `local/personas/main.md`.
+3. `local/README.md`, `local/DESIGN.md`, and `local/protocols/meta.md`.
+4. `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`, `ci.md`, `review.md`, `sessions.md`, and
+   `build-cache.md`.
+5. The 2026-08-31 re-hybridization entry in `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
+6. `results/telemetry/github-migration-map.md` and issue `#0007`.
+7. Every script named in the scope below and the shared data layer in
+   `local/bin/track.py`.
+
+Use the GitHub REST documentation for issues, sub-issues, pull requests,
+commit statuses, and pull-request reviews. The relevant fine-grained token
+permissions are Issues write, Pull requests write, Commit statuses write, and
+Contents write.
+
+## Operator decisions
+
+These points are adjudicated. Do not leave them as OPEN items.
+
+### 1. Authority and degraded mode
+
+- GitHub is the normal human-facing record after this change lands.
+- Local issue and PR files are always written and remain sufficient to run the
+  local lifecycle while GitHub is unavailable.
+- A successful local mutation followed by a remote failure is not rolled back.
+  Record the remote operation as pending, print an actionable warning, and
+  leave enough state for deterministic reconciliation.
+- Default mode is best effort so a link outage does not stop formalization.
+  Provide an explicit required-online mode for operators/tests that need a
+  nonzero exit when GitHub synchronization fails.
+- `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_ENABLED=false` is the literal kill switch. Unset means
+  enabled, matching the existing kill-switch convention.
+- Never log tokens or copy authentication material into the repository.
+
+### 2. Identity and idempotency
+
+- Extend issue and PR records with optional GitHub identity and synchronization
+  fields. At minimum retain the GitHub number, URL, and whether synchronization
+  is `synced` or `pending`; retain the numeric GitHub issue id when needed for
+  the sub-issue API.
+- Do not use one coarse synchronization flag for the entire record. Store
+  pending/synced state beside the operation's durable local evidence: issue
+  object/state/parent operations with the issue record, PR object/post-merge
+  operations with the PR record, commit-status publication with the per-SHA CI
+  manifest or a same-directory sidecar, and review publication with a per-SHA
+  review sidecar. Reconciliation must be able to distinguish these operations
+  after a process dies between any two of them.

+  payload digest, prerequisites, state (`pending`, `applying`, `synced`,
+  `superseded`, or `conflict`), attempt count, relevant remote id, timestamps,
+  and a classified last error. Distinguish at least `issue.ensure`,
+  `issue.parent`, `pr.head`, `pr.ensure`, `ci:<sha>:<context>`,
+  `review:<sha>:<digest>`, and `merge.main:<merge-sha>`.
+- Seed the existing mappings from
+  `results/telemetry/github-migration-map.md`; never recreate those records.
+- Every remotely created object carries a hidden stable marker based on the
+  local id, for example `mipstarre-local-issue:0007` or
+  `mipstarre-local-pr:0004`.
+- Before every create attempt, and again after an ambiguous failure, search the
+  authoritative REST listing for the marker. Do not rely on eventually
+  consistent search indexing. Adopt a unique match; treat multiple matches as
+  a conflict requiring operator attention.
+- Repeated synchronization after success must be a no-op except for deliberate
+  field/body/state updates.

+  adapter under `local/bin/`; do not duplicate ad hoc `gh` fragments across
+  shell scripts.
+- Invoke the REST API through `gh api`. Support an explicit executable override
+  such as `MIPSTARRE_GH` so deterministic tests can supply a fake CLI.
+- Resolve the repository from `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` or the `github` remote,
+  and retain `Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A` as the documented default.
+- Retry bounded transient failures with short exponential backoff. Tests must
+  be able to set delays to zero.
+- Retry connection failures, timeouts, `429`, and `5xx`; retain permanent
+  authentication, validation, and other `4xx` failures as pending or conflict
+  without wasting the full retry budget.

+  authenticated API probe rather than trusting `gh auth status`: the installed
+  `gh 2.4.0` reports a valid fine-grained PAT as invalid even though
+  `gh api user` succeeds. Missing CLI, authentication, or connectivity is a
+  loud pending-sync state, not silent success and not loss of the local record.

+  all pending records. Reconciliation is the recovery path after an offline or
+  ambiguous operation.
+- This adapter does not import arbitrary human edits made directly on GitHub.
+  Lifecycle scripts remain the mutation entry points for tool-owned title,
+  body, label, state, and gate fields. Document that boundary rather than
+  inventing an implicit last-writer-wins policy.
+
+### 4. Issue lifecycle

+- `issue_new.py` allocates and completes the local create/classify/scout stages
+  first, then ensures the GitHub issue exists with the final title, body, and
+  labels.

+  labels; do not let one absent label abort issue creation.

+  records exist, use GitHub's sub-issue endpoint to attach the child. A pending
+  parent leaves an explicit pending relation for reconciliation.

+  `completed`. It must be safe to retry even when the local issue is already
+  closed.
+- Remote issue bodies may expose the local id, but generated cross-reference
+  footers must use mapped GitHub numbers so `#N` never points to an unrelated
+  issue or pull request.
+
+### 5. Pull-request publication and the empty-branch case

+  opened before the implementation commit exists.
+- Enforce one open local PR record per branch. A repeated invocation must reuse
+  or report the existing record rather than allocate a second local identity.

+  `pr_open.py` creates the local record, marks remote creation pending, and says
+  exactly why. It is not an error and must not manufacture a placeholder
+  commit.

+  and creates or updates the GitHub PR. `ci.sh` may ensure this publication
+  before posting its status.
+- Narrow the old push rule explicitly: feature branches may be pushed as PR
+  heads; GitHub `main` may advance only after the local merge gate passes.
+- Translate `Addresses`/`Closes` footers from local issue ids to mapped GitHub
+  issue numbers in the remote PR body.
+
+### 6. Same-head CI status
+
+- `ci.sh` publishes a stable context such as `MIPStarRE/local-ci` for the exact
+  `HEAD_SHA` in its manifest. Publish `pending` when the run begins and the
+  final `success`, `failure`, or `error` after the complete manifest is written.
+- Partial/debug runs must not publish a success status.
+- Before posting, ensure the commit exists in the remote repository. Never
+  attach a result to a different or merely current branch head.
+- Recheck the actual local branch tip immediately before final publication;
+  re-reading only `pr.md` is insufficient if a commit lands during CI.
+- An ambiguous status POST is reconciled by reading the latest status with the
+  same SHA and context before retrying.
+- A remote publication failure does not rewrite the local CI conclusion. It
+  leaves GitHub synchronization pending and is recoverable from the manifest.
+
+### 7. Same-head review publication
+
+- After `review.sh` writes its local verdict files and rechecks the final head,
+  publish one review summary tied explicitly to that `HEAD_SHA`.
+- The GitHub account that opens these PRs cannot approve its own PR. Therefore
+  publish a GitHub `COMMENT` review for every local verdict and state clearly
+  that `APPROVED`, `COMMENTED`, or `CHANGES_REQUESTED` is the local gate verdict.
+  Do not pretend a GitHub self-approval succeeded.
+- Include the exact commit id in the review API request and verify the remote PR
+  head first. A mismatch is a refused/pending publication, never a review on a
+  stale or different head.
+- Recheck both `pr.md` and the actual local branch tip after the reviewers
+  finish, before updating local review state or publishing remotely.
+- Include a stable local-PR/head/digest marker. Repeating an identical publish
+  is a no-op; a materially different rerun on the same head remains auditable.
+- Preserve code/prose lane artifacts locally. The GitHub summary may combine
+  them, but it must report the worst local verdict and unresolved finding count.
+
+### 8. Merge and push ordering
+
+- `pr_merge.py` continues to run the unchanged local gate and perform the local
+  no-fast-forward merge. No remote operation may bypass `run_gate`.
+- Strengthen `run_gate` to parse the exact CI manifest and verify its SHA,
+  `partial: false`, and successful conclusion. Existence alone is not evidence.
+  If `--allow-unreviewed` is used, record that waiver durably as its help text
+  promises.
+- Before changing history, persist a merge intent containing the base tip and
+  reviewed head. Reconciliation may complete publication of that merge but
+  must never execute the merge a second time.
+- Replace `github-sync.sh`'s broad `git push --all` with a bounded,
+  retry-hardened push of explicit intended refs. Feature-head publication is
+  owned by the adapter; the post-merge default is `main`.
+- After the local merge, push `main`; GitHub should then recognize the PR as
+  merged from commit ancestry. Do not close it through the issue endpoint,
+  which would record a closed-unmerged PR.
+- If the post-merge push fails, keep the local merge and record remote sync as
+  pending. Report that the merge already happened and direct the operator to
+  reconciliation; do not invite a second merge attempt.
+- Resolve an ambiguous push by comparing remote `main` with the recorded merge

+  conflict rather than forcing an update.
+- Do not delete a remote feature branch until GitHub recognizes the merge. A

+  recovery metadata is durable.

+### 9. Protocol and telemetry consistency

+- Append an `EVOLUTION.md` implementation entry citing the owner decision and

+- Preserve local registry locks, atomic writes, primary-checkout ownership, and

+
+## Required tests

+

+3. Missing CLI, unauthenticated CLI, transient retry exhaustion, required-online

+4. Pending and final same-head commit statuses, identical retry suppression,

+5. Review publication with `event=COMMENT`, exact `commit_id`, identical retry

+   ambiguous main pushes, and remote divergence.
+7. Seed mappings for GitHub issues `#1` through `#4` and PR `#5` are adopted

+8. `local/bin/validate_tree.py` still accepts the extended record schema.
+

+change unless CI's change gating requires it.
+
+## Deliverable and report
+
+Commit the implementation on the issue branch with an imperative conventional
+subject. The final orchestrator report must list:

+- files and contracts changed;
+- exact fake-`gh` tests run and results;
+- local tree/CI checks run and results;

item.text:
## Findings

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `local/bin/ci.sh:529` — `--base` can target the PR head, skip every gate, and publish fully green CI
- [ ] F2 (blocker) `local/bin/ci.sh:1206` — final publication rechecks only HEAD, allowing CI steps to mutate tracked files and certify uncommitted bytes
- [ ] F3 (blocker) `local/bin/ci.sh:1218` — CI publishes its success summary before the mandatory manifest comment
- [ ] F4 (blocker) `local/bin/review.sh:1036` — an APPROVED trailer produces green review evidence even with unresolved blocker or changes findings
- [ ] F5 (blocker) `local/bin/agent.sh:289` — an issue without a branch receives a write-enabled session on main with permission to commit
- [ ] F6 (blocker) `local/bin/issue_close.py:58` — issue_close can close a pull request through GitHub's shared issues endpoint
- [ ] F7 (blocker) `local/bin/pr_merge.py:417` — the merge lock does not exclude concurrent CI, review, or autofix evidence mutations
- [ ] F8 (blocker) `local/bin/autofix.sh:452` — autofix ignores local-ci/summary and can dispatch from stale failed step statuses during a CI rerun
- [ ] F9 (blocker) `local/bin/autofix.sh:511` — review-fix trusts a body marker without requiring the review's commit_id to equal HEAD_SHA
- [ ] F10 (blocker) `local/bin/autofix.sh:884` — a successful fix reruns CI but leaves the bot head permanently without an exact-head review
- [ ] F11 (changes) `local/bin/autofix.sh:559` — the cap ritual still does not remove the auto-fix label required by the normative protocol
- [ ] F12 (changes) `local/bin/issue_new.py:96` — lossy title slugs silently alias distinct issues as the same idempotent creation
- [ ] F13 (changes) `local/bin/review.sh:1013` — every review writes a tracked telemetry file after cleanliness checks, dirtying or advancing the reviewed lifecycle
- [ ] F14 (changes) `local/personas/scout.md:22` — the scout persona promises GitHub comment publication that dispatch.sh never performs
- [ ] F15 (changes) `local/personas/orchestrator.md:95` — active personas still require deleted local issue files and deny the restored GitHub issue surface
- [ ] F16 (changes) `local/briefs/0007-github-native-workflow-brief.md:11` — the active brief requires a local write-through registry that this PR deletes
- [ ] F17 (changes) `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md:239` — the protocol amendment omits the required Change and Expected effect fields

## Review

**F1.** With `--base "$BRANCH"`, the merge base equals `HEAD_SHA`, the changed-file set is empty, all eight jobs become skipped-success, and the merge gate accepts the resulting statuses. Publishing runs must use the GitHub PR base; an override must be non-publishing.

**F2.** The initial cleanliness check is insufficient. In particular, `blueprint_lean_sync.py --update-lean-decls` can rewrite tracked `blueprint/lean_decls`; the final check sees the same commit SHA and certifies those modified bytes. Recheck cleanliness before publishing any success.

**F3.** If manifest-comment publication fails, `ci.sh` exits nonzero but leaves every merge-required status green. Publish the manifest first and `local-ci/summary` last.

**F4.** Both this condition and `pr_merge.py:176` treat `APPROVED` as unconditional. A malformed reviewer response containing blocker findings and an APPROVED trailer therefore merges. Parsed blocker/changes findings must force failure regardless of the trailer.

**F5.** `TRUSTED_REF` defaults to `main`, while the generated prompt explicitly permits commits. This bypasses the exclusive PR/CI/review merge path in `local/protocols/issues-prs.md:78-79`. Writable issue sessions must require an issue branch.

**F6.** GitHub's issues endpoint also returns pull requests. No `pull_request` check precedes the PATCH, so `issue_close.py N` can close PR N without merging it. Fetch and reject PR-shaped records first.

**F7.** The exact-SHA merge guard protects head bytes, not mutable statuses. A concurrent CI run can replace green evidence with pending or failure after the gate read but before the merge PUT. Merge and lifecycle publishers need shared exclusion through the irreversible operation.

**F8.** CI marks its summary pending before replacing old per-step statuses. Autofix discards that summary and can act on an old build failure while CI is reading the same worktree. Require a terminal exact-head summary failure before dispatch.

**F9.** The marker includes a SHA, but it is not proof that the review is attached to that SHA. Require both the marker and `row.commit_id == HEAD_SHA` before authorizing a write-enabled fixer.

**F10.** After a fix, only CI runs; `review.sh` skips bot commits, and the next autofix invocation can exit “nothing to fix” before cap handling. The resulting green bot head cannot satisfy the exact-head review gate. The terminal successful fix needs one forced review.

**F11.** `local/protocols/autofix.md:163-169` requires removing `auto-fix-codex` at the cap. The repair standardized the label name but never implemented removal.

**F12.** `slugify` truncates and normalizes titles, while adoption does not compare title, body, or labels. Distinct issues can therefore reuse an old issue and even attach it to the wrong parent. Require an explicit key or reject mismatched adoption.

**F13.** The current head, which commits the prior review ledger, demonstrates the feedback loop. Review artifacts should remain in runtime storage or use a defined out-of-band archival path that neither dirties the merge worktree nor changes the reviewed head.

**F14-F17.** The operative documentation remains internally inconsistent: scout output is not published, several personas reference retired issue files, the new brief specifies the opposite authority model, and the amendment does not follow `local/protocols/meta.md:36-40`. These must be synchronized and covered by the hygiene tests.

No Lean, blueprint, or paper-gap declarations changed, so source-statement fidelity and proof-debt checks are not applicable. `git diff --check`, shell syntax checking, and AST parsing of all extant changed Python files passed. I did not rerun the temporary-file-writing test suite in the read-only reviewer sandbox; the supplied exact-head CI status reports success. Prior round findings explicitly deferred to follow-up issues were not duplicated here.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED
